limitations: Full-fit measurements: one Nautilus stage of one SLaM chain per record, never a per-likelihood cost; the sampler is <sampler>:<stage> because the key has no stage

wall_s is the sampler clock (samples_info.json) and includes sampler overhead; implied_ms_per_eval = wall_s / likelihood_evals * 1000 (implied_s_per_eval the same in seconds) is therefore an upper bound on the per-evaluation cost
parallel_efficiency is null: no 1-core row of any key exists yet
parity_status is not_assessed unless a declared ruling of record names the run (parity_basis); the exporter computes no parity verdict

likelihood_eval_s_search_summary is PyAutoFit's search.summary 'Log Likelihood Function Evaluation Time': one un-repeated call of the fitness at the max-likelihood point after the fit, so on a JAX leg it can include tracing or compilation; time_per_sample_s_search_summary is its 'Time Per Sample' (sampler time over total samples). Both are raw seconds
56 of 56 records carry search.summary timings (0 from the stage row, 56 from catalogue/search_summary_backfill.json); 0 have none

37 of 56 records pair with a profiling-summary@3 runtime record of the lens snapshot cached in catalogue/pulse_lens_runtime_reference.json on an exact (likelihood, instrument, setup_id, host_class, model_variant) match, the current record first, else the newest (profiling_status says which); profiling_per_call_s is Pulse's per-call time of that record, predicted_ms_per_eval the same in ms; unmatched: 7 no profiling runtime record with model_variant light_fixed; 12 no profiling runtime record with setup_id jax_cpu_dense_fp64

size_match compares the run's source pixels (rectangular mesh_shape product, Delaunay mesh_pixels Hilbert vertices) with the profiling record's size bin: 4 match, 33 differ (a different-size likelihood than the run's), 0 unknown because a side records no count
